title: How Tibo built Tweet Hunter, sold for $8M, then ran five co-maker startups past $400k/month
summary: Tibo explains his shift from ego-driven, VC-funded failures to building revenue-first products. He covers the equity-for-influencer launch that took Tweet Hunter from 3K to 20K MRR in two weeks and his co-maker model of rescuing stuck products with distribution. He also shares retention lessons from Outrank and what he'd change in an exit.

principles.text: Build for revenue and a good living, not to impress people; chasing ego metrics hid the fact that nothing was working.
principles.quote: just trying to make a good living out of the product we're building.

principles.text: Give a big influencer real equity as a co-founder and let them launch it to their audience; it can multiply MRR in weeks.
principles.quote: just this launch, I think in two weeks, we got from 3K in monthly revenue to 20K.

principles.text: Market the outcome (more business, more money), not the feature layer; it multiplied conversion.
principles.quote: And by by embracing that approach and just changing a little bit our marketing, it worked like 10 times more.

principles.text: Partner on others' stuck products: motivation is higher on their own idea. Fix the core with a few users, then add distribution.
principles.quote: if you reach out on an existing project, it's his ID. Like the the guy is going to be crazy motivated no matter what because it's it's his ID.

principles.text: Talk to users directly to learn their workflow, then design the product so it works without discipline from them (auto-publish).
principles.quote: If you do not come to the software, no matter what, it's going to be published anyway.

principles.text: Validate by building a prototype in days and putting it in front of relevant users rather than describing the idea.
principles.quote: it's 10 times more efficient when you have an idea to quickly build it in two days and put it in the hands of people who are relevant to use this ID and give you feedback.
